text:
Mira: Heads-up — we need a quick alignment on post-launch priorities for the inference dashboard. Customer A (large fintech) pushed three bugs + two feature asks that would change UX. They flagged SLA risk if not addressed in next 2 weeks.

Jon: Can you list the three bugs and their impact?

Mira: Sure — short list: 1) dropdown for model selection sometimes resets during long sessions (intermittent, high touch). 2) cost telemetry double-counts tokens on retry paths (affects billing reports). 3) streaming websocket occasionally stalls on reconnect (sporadic, impacts latency-sensitive apps). Feature asks: a) per-route default batching toggle, b) CSV export for token-level breakdowns.

Alex: I think the dropdown bug is high priority — affects demos and signups. Streaming websocket looks bad for low-latency customers too. Cost telemetry is high-impact for finance but might be fixable with a data backfill.

Kevin: Agree. Proposal: triage into A/B/C — A = user-facing regressions and SLA risk, B = billing correctness / analytics, C = quality-of-life new features. Put dropdown + websocket as A, telemetry as B, features as C.

Sylvia: For A items, do we have owners and estimated effort? We should avoid blocking Dedicated rollouts.

Mira: Owners: Alex owns dropdown, Kevin owns websocket (eng-runtime), Jon will own telemetry backfill (eng-platform). Rough rigs: dropdown ~2 dev-days + 1 QA day, websocket ~3-4 dev-days + infra testing, telemetry ~2 dev-days + data infra work (maybe longer). Features: batching toggle ~3 dev-days + config surface, CSV export ~2 days frontend.

Jon: If we follow a two-lane approach — lane 1 = 2-week hotpath (A items); lane 2 = continuous backlog for B/C — do we have capacity? We can earmark 40% of eng cycles for lane 1 for next sprint.

Alex: 40% sounds tight. Recommend 60% for lane 1 this sprint given customer SLA. We can cut scope for features.

Kevin: Caveat — websocket fix needs integration test with the new connection pooling change from last release. That may add time. Suggest a quick canary: patch + rollout to customer A account first.

Mira: Canary plan sounds good. Steps: 1) small fix PR -> 2) deploy to canary (customer-A namespace) -> 3) observe 24h metrics (latency, reconnects) -> 4) full rollout. Can deploy-bot run the canary?

deploy-bot: Canary job queued: build 2.2.1-canary -> staging -> customer-A. Use flag `--canary-namespace=customer-a`.

Sylvia: For prioritization, let's add a simple scoring rubric: Severity (3/2/1), Customer impact (3 if enterprise), Effort (1 low - 3 high, lower better). Score = Severity + CustomerImpact - Effort. We can threshold >3 = lane 1.

Jon: Quick calc: dropdown (3 + 3 - 1 = 5) -> lane1. Websocket (3 + 3 - 2 = 4) -> lane1. Telemetry (2 + 3 - 2 = 3) -> borderline lane2 unless billing is trending.

Alex: Also check rollback safety and test coverage — if a fix risks regressions, factor that into effort.

Mira: Decision: allocate 60% capacity to lane1 for next sprint, do canary for websocket, immediate patch for dropdown, telemetry will be scheduled as lane2 but with a monitoring alert to escalate if billing error rate increases. Features (batching toggle, CSV) deferred to next sprint unless customers sign up for premium changes.

Kevin: I’ll start the canary run and open PRs with `fix/dropdown-reset` and `fix/ws-reconnect`. Please add testing checklists to PR descriptions.

Alex: I'll pick up dropdown PR review and write a short e2e that simulates long sessions.

Jon: I'll scope telemetry mitigation: create a one-off job to dedupe retries in the next 48h and add a dashboard.

Sylvia: I'll update the roadmap board and mark these as "customer-A driven" and add the scoring column so PMs can see triage.

Mira: Acceptance criteria for sprint: dropdown fixed and verified in canary + no regressions; websocket reduced reconnects by >=50% in canary; telemetry alerting in place. If any fail, escalate to incident channel and pull more resources.

Alex: Quick note — we should create a short postmortem checklist to capture root cause and small followups so these don't reoccur.

Kevin: Agreed. I'll add `doc/postlaunch-debt-capture.md` to the PR template.

Mira: Thanks all. If no objections, I’ll ship this plan and sync with CS to manage customer expectations. :thumbsup:

Jon: :thumbsup:

Sylvia: :thumbsup:

Alex: :thumbsup:

Kevin: Starting work now.

Mira: I'll follow up with a 15-minute sync tomorrow to confirm owners and blockers.
